procedure.description: suction assisted lipectomy, trunk and lower extremities, for lipedema

denial.carcText: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 15877 (suction assisted lipectomy, trunk and lower extremities, for lipedema) with date of service 2026-02-02. CARC 56: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer. RARC N130: Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service. Payer remark: Liposuction for lipedema is investigational under the plan and is not covered.

criteria.text: Liposuction for lipedema is considered investigational and is not a covered benefit under this plan under any circumstances.

chart.text: Blood pressure check. 119 over 83 today, 137 over 76 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.

55 year old woman here about her legs, self-referred after reading about lipedema. Mother and aunt had the same legs. Discussed lymph-sparing liposuction, staged, and that it is debulking, not a cure. Her history otherwise: mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, seasonal allergies, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Surgeries: wisdom teeth. Allergies: no drug allergies. Quit smoking 7 years ago, no alcohol, stays home with the kids. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today.
Vitamin D came back 17. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Follow-up. Reviewed photos and measurements, legs unchanged. Went over the staged plan and the compression afterward. Vitals today 125 over 68, pulse 69.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 5 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Here with a cough and congestion for 4 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 14 and 13. No ocular pathology noted.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 233, LDL 138, HDL 52, triglycerides 106. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.5, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 50. Repeat in a year.
Pre-op for stage one, thighs. Consent signed. Marked standing. Garments ordered.

expected.note: Plan exclusion: crit-1 (coverage) cannot be met by any chart content.
